title: What is the projection of a tilted square card?
description: A square card of side five centimetres is tilted about one side so that the opposite side is three centimetres higher. The board keeps the two flat sides, finds the projection of the two leaning sides with the right triangle rule, and names the shape. Keeko's doubt is that the projection is still a square.
teaching_notes: One idea: a projection is built from the projections of the sides, so the sides parallel to the floor keep their length and the leaning sides become shorter. Watch for students who think a card keeps its shape on the floor.

source: A square card of side 5 cm is tilted about one of its sides
video_script.why: The child finds the projection of a tilted card by projecting each side, because the sides parallel to the floor keep their length and each leaning side forms a right triangle with its height gap.
video_script.substitution: square of side 5 cm; two sides parallel to the floor stay 5 cm; each leaning side projects to square root of (5 x 5 - 3 x 3) = square root of 16 = 4 cm; parallel sides stay parallel and the angles at the hinge stay right angles; rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm.
video_script.anchor: the square card tilted about its lower side, seen from the side and from above
video_script.wrong_answer: the card does not change size, so the projection is still a square of five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the projection is still a 5 by 5 square; seen from the side, each leaning side rises 3 cm and covers only 4 cm of floor, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The projection is a rectangle, five centimetres by four centimetres

final_answer.spoken: a rectangle, five centimetres by four centimetres

names.Ziva: the theorem used for the shortest path of 40 cm

maths_rules: the projection of an object is made by dropping every place of it straight down onto the plane, at a right angle
the projection of a polygon is made of the projections of its sides
the two sides parallel to the floor keep their length of 5 cm
each leaning side is 5 cm long and rises 3 cm; its projection squared = 5 x 5 - 3 x 3 = 25 - 9 = 16
its projection = square root of 16 = 4 cm
parallel sides stay parallel, and the angles at the hinge stay right angles, so the projection is a rectangle 5 cm by 4 cm
video_script.design: One idea: project the sides one by one. The card tilts on the stage; the flat sides keep their colour and the leaning sides are drawn with their height gap and projection in the accent colour.

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, each leaning side is five centimetres long and rises three centimetres. It is the longest side of a right triangle.

<bookmark mark='work'/>The square of its projection is five times five take away three times three. That is twenty five take away nine, which is sixteen.
